description: Cross-language golden fixture for S2 signal emission (INT-3, #1394 S2 aligned). Single source of truth for the 14-event list: the Go side keeps an in-code emitter table (F8 precedent, task-transitions.json) and cross-checks it against this file in tests; the Python side reads this file at runtime. Precedent: task-transitions.json.
id_rule: event_id = 'ev_' + sha256(team_id|project_id|task_id|loop_id|event_type|source_event|iteration|fingerprint|attempt|audit_seq)[:16] hex. Fixed field order; each field is a plain string, empty string when the emitter carries no such identity (project-level events leave task_id empty; task events set project_id and leave loop_id/iteration empty; iteration is the decimal iteration_index or empty). fingerprint = the event fingerprint field = hex(sha256 of the ref bytes after the main write) - the stable identity of the logical operation's result. audit_seq = the project's persisted committed-operation revision (project meta 'audit_seq'; 0 when absent): advanced by exactly one on each committed Go intervention write (markAuditFields + conditional ETag write), it is the persistent identity of the operation INSTANCE. A retry of the same operation re-reads the same committed revision and the same state bytes, so it re-lands on the same id (consumers dedupe by event_id, keyed on the operation identity per #1394), while two distinct operations - another project, another loop iteration, or a second occurrence of the same control operation (pause/resume/pause within one wall-clock second, whose post-write state bytes are byte-identical at second-precision updated_at) - hash distinct inputs and cannot share a key. No raw timestamp is ever part of the identity; audit_seq, not the clock, distinguishes operation instances. Rejection family (SIG-MISMATCH): a rejection commits no state, so the ref bytes - and the fingerprint - are identical across distinct rejected operations on the same task state; those emitters append one extra final component `action|from|to` (the rejection discriminator) to the hash input. Distinct rejections therefore get distinct ids, while a retry of the same rejection re-hashes identically. Events without a discriminator hash the fixed ten-field input above unchanged (the cross-language fixed vector is unaffected; Go has no rejection emitter).
source_event_note: source_event = the row's row id, unique per emit point. It is hashed into id_rule, so two emit points must never share it (11-SIGNAL: submit and accept share source_event.origin=submit but use different source_events to keep ids distinct).

retention.description: S2 event store lifecycle (#1702). The live stream under shared/events/{team_id}/ is one immutable file per event; without cleanup it grows unboundedly while every list_events read pays O(N) file reads. Retention groups a project's live event files into content-addressed archive pieces once the project is terminal or expired, deletes the local source files, and prunes the MinIO mirror best-effort. The contract 'version' field above is the id_rule version (pinned by the cross-language fixed vector and the Go TestContractCoversAllEmitters), so registering this store-lifecycle section does not bump it.

triggers.project_completed: project meta status == 'completed' (the terminal lifecycle state written by Go CompleteProject and Python complete_project)
triggers.expired: project metadata, latest live event and associated task activity are all older than retention.days (default 7; configurable via TEAMHARNESS_RUNTIME_CONFIG retention.days, TEAMHARNESS_RETENTION_DAYS env override)

retention.attribution: an event file is attributed to a project via payload.project_id (every Python emitter stamps it), then the task meta's project_id for task-level events, then a shared/projects/{project_id}/ path in the event's ref (the Go read-side pattern); an event that cannot be attributed to a candidate project is left live forever

archive.shape: {archive: true, version: 1, team_id, project_id, archived_at (last write time), reason ('project_completed' | 'expired'), event_count, events: [the original 11-field event objects, (occurred_at, event_id) ascending]}
archive.merge_semantics: content-addressed pieces preserve different workspace subsets without overwrites; archive upload is retried even when a local piece already exists; each local source stays as its retry record until durable archive publication and remote source pruning both succeed
archive.stream_semantics: archive objects are NOT part of the live stream: both read surfaces (projectflow list_events and the controller's GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/signal-events) read live event files only, so archived events leave list_events results; the archive object is the retained audit copy (local + MinIO mirror) and both legacy daily and content-addressed archive names are skipped before content reads/downloads

retention.mirror_sync: the pruned source objects are removed from the MinIO mirror with filesync action delete (new in #1702); prune failures retain local source retry records and never block emission or reads; an object already absent counts as pruned
retention.execution_timing: at the tail of every Python signal event emit (an O(1) state-file check under shared/events/{team_id}/.retention.state; the full sweep runs every 16 emits) and lazily on every projectflow list_events call; a 24h max-lag backstop re-runs the sweep when the last one is older. list_events stays read-only with respect to project/task state (see durability.json notes).

fast_path.mechanism: event ids are sha256-based (id_rule above), so filename order is NOT time order; the fast path sorts the live event files by mtime (newest first), reads at most window_files = max(20, 4 * limit) of them, applies the same filters, and serves pages newest-first; the cursor anchor is the page's oldest event and the next page resumes strictly before it (same base64url(ts + NUL + id) encoding; recent-mode cursors only resume in recent mode)
fast_path.approximation: events in live files older than the window are not scanned: filtered queries may miss older matches, and page 1 is the newest events rather than the oldest ones. The response carries 'approximate': true whenever the window did not cover every live file; the default (exact) read is unchanged and remains the full-directory ascending stream shared with the Go read surface.
